241	## Sixteenth block: the assault rifle, from one Tripo mesh to a complete weapon
242	Owner's note (translated): "This is the game's assault rifle. I think it's a single mesh, and all the work it needs is ahead of it; you will do it. Animations, the colour change, the ammo panel, everything as you already know: it has to end up as a complete and absolutely functional weapon, with everything a game of this kind needs. Modify it in Blender or Unreal as you like. For code tasks, don't use Muse Spark, use Sonnet."
243	
244	**The source.** The owner's `carabina-roja.zip` held a Tripo GLB. It is one mesh of about 1,000 loose panels and 5,498 triangles, 1.0 m long. It came with a 4096 albedo and a `neon_mask` that marks where it glows.
245	- It had **no magazine** and no separate moving parts.
246	- The architect (Claude Opus 5.5) did the art headless in Blender 5.3.0, without asking. Scripts:
247	  - `Tools/Blender/rifle_import_glb.py`: GLB to `SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend`, the one source;
248	  - `rifle_export_fbx.py`;
249	  - `Tools/Jam/Import-Rifle.ps1` and `import_rifle.py`, with the same one-source rule as the pistol.
250	
251	**The parts and how each was chosen.** The rifle has five meshes in `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Rifle`.
252	- **Trigger:** the blade's panels, picked by their bounding box inside the guard. Its origin is at the hinge, so it rotates -8° like the pistol's.
253	- **Magazine:** new geometry modelled by script, because the model had none and a rifle needs one to reload.
254	  - A curved box under the stub in front of the trigger guard, with a base plate.
255	  - A glowing slit on each side, in the element colour.
256	  - On reload it slides out 17 cm, then back in.
257	- **Weak-point light:** the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight. They are off normally and flash on a head or weak-point hit, the pistol's rule.
258	- **Ammo display:** a 2:1 hologram pane just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player. It is the pistol's shared `M_GunHolo`, with its own text layout: no frame or dots to avoid, so the number is larger.
259	- **Energy bar:** no separate mesh. The body's second UV map carries the position along the side neon strip, and `M_RifleAtlas` cuts the strip into 13 cells with thin dark gaps.
260	  - They drain from the muzzle end with the enchant's time left: the same "+ half a cell" rule and the same code as the pistol.
261	  - The rest of the neon glows in the element colour all the time: idle mint (the model's own colour), or the enchant's element.
262	- **Problems found by the import checks:**
263	  - The FBX import flips V, so the "on the strip" flag in UV 1 came out inverted. The check that counts strip vertices caught it.
264	  - The magazine's three material slots collapsed into one. A new check now requires 3 slots.
265	  - Both were fixed in the export script before any code used them.
266	- **Textures:** the 4096 maps are capped at 2048 in Unreal.
267	
268	**Code: Claude Sonnet 5.5 at High effort.** The owner set it as the implementer for this chat, so not Muse Spark. Brief: `Prompts/feedback12_rifle_viewmodel.md`.
269	- The pistol-only viewmodel code became one code path for both guns. A small art description per model (folder, parts, offsets, scale, idle glow, muzzle tip, display layout) is chosen by `ViewModel` in `Weapons.json`.
270	- New for both guns:
271	  - **Shot kick:** the viewmodel moves back and tips up, then eases back over 0.09 s. It is the look only; aim and camera are untouched.
272	  - **Muzzle flash:** a 0.05 s glowing star at the muzzle in the glow colour.
273	- The rifle sits at scale 0.62, tuned by Sonnet over several smoke screenshots.
274	- The smoke run has new rifle steps, all green:
275	  - `meshes=5`;
276	  - display `30` → `29` → `--`;
277	  - magazine out 17.1 cm;
278	  - weak-point flash 1.00 → 0.00, and 0.00 on a body shot;
279	  - half bar 0.52;
280	  - muzzle flash and kick on both guns.
281	  - Every pistol line is unchanged.
282	- One deviation, reported by Sonnet: the smoke run applies the rifle's enchant as a status directly, because the enchant spell is still on cooldown from the pistol step.
283	- The architect looked at the screenshots: the rifle is in the lower right, the number reads upright, and the flash sits at the muzzle. Accepted.
284	- **Owner, after the screenshot (translated):** "The rifle closer to the screen", then "the front pointing at the crosshair, a little closer and to the left". Done directly by the architect, because these are values in the rifle's art description:
285	  - root offset (30, 2, 1) → (14, 2, 1) → (8, -3, 2) cm;
286	  - yaw -5° → -10°;
287	  - checked on `media/2026-11-12/14b_rifle_hip_closer.png`: the barrel now runs to the crosshair, and "30" is about twice as large.
288	- Package `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`: 252.8 MB.
289	- **Owner, second note (translated):** "The weapon is still too far away in the frame, bring it closer. Its alignment doesn't go straight to the crosshair: look at how rifles are framed in first-person shooters and adjust it. And look closely at the screenshots you sent: there are still imperfections on the rifle; find them and fix them."
290	  - **Framing.** The architect searched the web: Unreal answers, Leadwerks and Roblox developer threads, and CS2 viewmodel guides. At the hip, the weapon is held parallel to the view, or turned slightly towards the point the crosshair aims at. Perspective then makes the barrel converge on the screen centre. Our -10° yaw made the barrel cross the crosshair instead.
291	    - The rifle is now parallel to the view (yaw -0.4°, the angle that meets the crosshair at 15 m), 20 cm closer and 3 cm further left: root offset (-12, -6, 2) cm.
292	    - The barrel line now runs into the crosshair, and the sight with its ammo count sits in the lower right.
293	  - **Imperfections the architect found on enlarged crops of the screenshots, and the fixes:**
294	    1. The hologram pane spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main face. From the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight. It is now inside the rear face of the eyepiece, 1.5 mm in front of it.
295	    2. Right after the rifle was equipped it looked flat, blurry and tan: textures still streaming in at their lowest mip. The two rifle textures are now never streamed (about 5 MB resident).
296	    3. The 10 cm near plane cut the stock open at the bottom right. It is now 3 cm (`DefaultEngine.ini`, `NearClipPlane`), the usual fix for first-person weapons.
297	    4. The white polymer read washed out next to the pistol: albedo × 0.8.
298	  - **Tried and reverted:** a two-sided material, to guard against holes in the loose-panel mesh. The Tripo panels are doubled back to back and z-fought, so the whole rifle looked grainy. It stays one-sided, with the reason written in `import_rifle.py`.

## Sixteenth block: the assault rifle, from one Tripo mesh to a complete weapon
Owner's note (translated): "This is the game's assault rifle. I think it's a single mesh, and all the work it needs is ahead of it; you will do it. Animations, the colour change, the ammo panel, everything as you already know: it has to end up as a complete and absolutely functional weapon, with everything a game of this kind needs. Modify it in Blender or Unreal as you like. For code tasks, don't use Muse Spark, use Sonnet."

**The source.** The owner's `carabina-roja.zip` held a Tripo GLB. It is one mesh of about 1,000 loose panels and 5,498 triangles, 1.0 m long. It came with a 4096 albedo and a `neon_mask` that marks where it glows.
- It had **no magazine** and no separate moving parts.
- The architect (Claude Opus 5.5) did the art headless in Blender 5.3.0, without asking. Scripts:
  - `Tools/Blender/rifle_import_glb.py`: GLB to `SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend`, the one source;
  - `rifle_export_fbx.py`;
  - `Tools/Jam/Import-Rifle.ps1` and `import_rifle.py`, with the same one-source rule as the pistol.

**The parts and how each was chosen.** The rifle has five meshes in `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Rifle`.
- **Trigger:** the blade's panels, picked by their bounding box inside the guard. Its origin is at the hinge, so it rotates -8° like the pistol's.
- **Magazine:** new geometry modelled by script, because the model had none and a rifle needs one to reload.
  - A curved box under the stub in front of the trigger guard, with a base plate.
  - A glowing slit on each side, in the element colour.
  - On reload it slides out 17 cm, then back in.
- **Weak-point light:** the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight. They are off normally and flash on a head or weak-point hit, the pistol's rule.
- **Ammo display:** a 2:1 hologram pane just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player. It is the pistol's shared `M_GunHolo`, with its own text layout: no frame or dots to avoid, so the number is larger.
- **Energy bar:** no separate mesh. The body's second UV map carries the position along the side neon strip, and `M_RifleAtlas` cuts the strip into 13 cells with thin dark gaps.
  - They drain from the muzzle end with the enchant's time left: the same "+ half a cell" rule and the same code as the pistol.
  - The rest of the neon glows in the element colour all the time: idle mint (the model's own colour), or the enchant's element.
- **Problems found by the import checks:**
  - The FBX import flips V, so the "on the strip" flag in UV 1 came out inverted. The check that counts strip vertices caught it.
  - The magazine's three material slots collapsed into one. A new check now requires 3 slots.
  - Both were fixed in the export script before any code used them.
- **Textures:** the 4096 maps are capped at 2048 in Unreal.

**Code: Claude Sonnet 5.5 at High effort.** The owner set it as the implementer for this chat, so not Muse Spark. Brief: `Prompts/feedback12_rifle_viewmodel.md`.
- The pistol-only viewmodel code became one code path for both guns. A small art description per model (folder, parts, offsets, scale, idle glow, muzzle tip, display layout) is chosen by `ViewModel` in `Weapons.json`.
- New for both guns:
  - **Shot kick:** the viewmodel moves back and tips up, then eases back over 0.09 s. It is the look only; aim and camera are untouched.
  - **Muzzle flash:** a 0.05 s glowing star at the muzzle in the glow colour.
- The rifle sits at scale 0.62, tuned by Sonnet over several smoke screenshots.
- The smoke run has new rifle steps, all green:
  - `meshes=5`;
  - display `30` → `29` → `--`;
  - magazine out 17.1 cm;
  - weak-point flash 1.00 → 0.00, and 0.00 on a body shot;
  - half bar 0.52;
  - muzzle flash and kick on both guns.
  - Every pistol line is unchanged.
- One deviation, reported by Sonnet: the smoke run applies the rifle's enchant as a status directly, because the enchant spell is still on cooldown from the pistol step.
- The architect looked at the screenshots: the rifle is in the lower right, the number reads upright, and the flash sits at the muzzle. Accepted.
- **Owner, after the screenshot (translated):** "The rifle closer to the screen", then "the front pointing at the crosshair, a little closer and to the left". Done directly by the architect, because these are values in the rifle's art description:
  - root offset (30, 2, 1) → (14, 2, 1) → (8, -3, 2) cm;
  - yaw -5° → -10°;
  - checked on `media/2026-11-12/14b_rifle_hip_closer.png`: the barrel now runs to the crosshair, and "30" is about twice as large.
- Package `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`: 252.8 MB.
- **Owner, second note (translated):** "The weapon is still too far away in the frame, bring it closer. Its alignment doesn't go straight to the crosshair: look at how rifles are framed in first-person shooters and adjust it. And look closely at the screenshots you sent: there are still imperfections on the rifle; find them and fix them."
  - **Framing.** The architect searched the web: Unreal answers, Leadwerks and Roblox developer threads, and CS2 viewmodel guides. At the hip, the weapon is held parallel to the view, or turned slightly towards the point the crosshair aims at. Perspective then makes the barrel converge on the screen centre. Our -10° yaw made the barrel cross the crosshair instead.
    - The rifle is now parallel to the view (yaw -0.4°, the angle that meets the crosshair at 15 m), 20 cm closer and 3 cm further left: root offset (-12, -6, 2) cm.
    - The barrel line now runs into the crosshair, and the sight with its ammo count sits in the lower right.
  - **Imperfections the architect found on enlarged crops of the screenshots, and the fixes:**
    1. The hologram pane spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main face. From the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight. It is now inside the rear face of the eyepiece, 1.5 mm in front of it.
    2. Right after the rifle was equipped it looked flat, blurry and tan: textures still streaming in at their lowest mip. The two rifle textures are now never streamed (about 5 MB resident).
    3. The 10 cm near plane cut the stock open at the bottom right. It is now 3 cm (`DefaultEngine.ini`, `NearClipPlane`), the usual fix for first-person weapons.
    4. The white polymer read washed out next to the pistol: albedo × 0.8.
  - **Tried and reverted:** a two-sided material, to guard against holes in the loose-panel mesh. The Tripo panels are doubled back to back and z-fought, so the whole rifle looked grainy. It stays one-sided, with the reason written in `import_rifle.py`.
  - Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/14c_rifle_hip_framed.png` (idle) and `14d_rifle_enchanted.png` (lightning enchant, half bar).
- **Owner, third note (translated):** "In the screenshots you sent, the weapon looks like it's made of jelly." The architect found three causes:
  1. **Lost normals.** The Tripo GLB carries custom normals, and the export's bmesh round trip dropped them. Every face was then smooth-shaded, so the hard-surface gun rendered soft and rounded. Fix: edges sharper than 30° are now shaded hard (`set_sharp_from_angle` in `rifle_export_fbx.py`).
  2. **One flat material value.** Roughness 0.42 and metallic 0.15 covered the whole gun, so it looked soft and glossy. The source has no roughness map. The albedo's brightness now tells polymer from metal: light parts are matte polymer (roughness 0.68, not metallic), dark parts satin metal (0.36, metallic 0.6).
  3. **No self-shadow.** The viewmodel parts cast no shadow at all, so nothing shaded anything else. They are now "self shadow only": the gun shades itself (the sight now drops a shadow on the receiver) but casts nothing on the world. This applies to the pistol too; checked on `13a`, which is unchanged apart from its own shading.
  - The rifle textures went back to full 4096 (no streaming), because the parts nearest the camera were blurry at 2048. The package grew from 252.8 to 256 MB.
  - **Note on the smoke screenshots:** `14a` comes out tan and grainy whenever the rifle material has just changed. That is the editor's fallback material while shaders compile. The packaged game ships compiled shaders, so it does not happen there.
  - Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/14f_rifle_solid.png`, `14g_rifle_solid_enchanted.png`.
- **To check by playing:**
  - The framing. The stock now goes under the HUD weapon box at the bottom right.
  - Whether "30" is readable.
  - The look while aiming.
  - The feel of full-auto kick.
  - The strip draining over a real enchant.

1	# Exports the assault rifle (Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend, one Tripo mesh made of ~1000 loose
2	# panels) as static-mesh FBX files for Unreal, plus its two textures. The game animates the moving parts in code.
3	#   SM_Rifle_Body            everything that does not move. UV 1 ("ImbueU") drives the energy strip: U = 0 at the
4	#                            muzzle end of the side neon strip, 1 at its rear end; V = 1 marks glow that is not part of
5	#                            the strip (always lit). M_RifleAtlas splits the strip into 13 cells, like the pistol bar.
6	#   SM_Rifle_Trigger         the trigger blade inside the guard, pivot at its top (hinge)
7	#   SM_Rifle_Magazine        NEW geometry modelled here (the source has no magazine): a curved box magazine under the
8	#                            magazine well in front of the trigger guard, base plate and a glowing slit on each side
9	#   SM_Rifle_WeakPointLight  the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight (lit only on weak-point hits)
10	#   SM_Rifle_AmmoDisplay     a 2:1 quad just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player, for the ammo count
11	# Source frame: muzzle at -Y, up +Z, metres, ~1.0 m long. Export frame: turned +90 deg around Z so the muzzle points
12	# to +X (Unreal forward), origin at the hand point (top of the pistol grip). Same FBX settings as the pistol.
13	# Usage: blender -b Rifle.blend --python rifle_export_fbx.py -- <out_dir>
14	import bpy, bmesh, sys, os, json, math
15	from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
16	
17	argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
18	out_dir = argv[0]
19	os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "Export"), exist_ok=True)
20	os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "Textures"), exist_ok=True)
21	
22	scene = bpy.context.scene
23	SRC = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"][0]
24	CX = -0.0055                       # the model's centre line in X (its left and right panels mirror around it)
25	HAND = Vector((CX, 0.19, 0.0))     # top of the pistol grip
26	TRIGGER_PIVOT = Vector((CX, 0.125, 0.003))
27	MAG_PIVOT = Vector((CX, 0.032, -0.028))
28	MAG_OUT = Vector((0.0, -0.02, -0.17))   # slide-out vector of the magazine on reload, source frame
29	TURN = Matrix.Rotation(math.pi / 2, 4, "Z")
30	SHARP_ANGLE = 30.0   # degrees: edges sharper than this are shaded hard
31	# Neon strip span along Y (source frame): from its muzzle end to its rear end, below the sight.
32	STRIP_Y0, STRIP_Y1, STRIP_ZMAX = -0.345, 0.085, 0.1
33	
34	
35	def islands(bm):
36	    seen, out = set(), []
37	    for f in bm.faces:
38	        if f.index in seen:
39	            continue
40	        stack, comp = [f], []
41	        seen.add(f.index)
42	        while stack:
43	            a = stack.pop()
44	            comp.append(a.index)
45	            for e in a.edges:
46	                for b in e.link_faces:
47	                    if b.index not in seen:
48	                        seen.add(b.index)
49	                        stack.append(b)
50	        out.append(comp)
51	    return out
52	
53	
54	def inside(vs, lo, hi):
55	    return all(lo[i] <= min(v.co[i] for v in vs) and max(v.co[i] for v in vs) <= hi[i] for i in range(3))
56	
57	
58	# Pick the trigger and the lenses by the bounding box of their loose panels.
59	src_bm = bmesh.new()
60	src_bm.from_mesh(SRC.data)
61	src_bm.faces.ensure_lookup_table()
62	TRIGGER_FACES, LENS_FACES = set(), set()
63	for comp in islands(src_bm):
64	    vs = {v for i in comp for v in src_bm.faces[i].verts}
65	    if inside(vs, (-0.0105, 0.116, -0.043), (-0.0005, 0.134, 0.0035)):
66	        TRIGGER_FACES.update(comp)
67	    elif len(comp) >= 15 and inside(vs, (-0.042, 0.104, 0.105), (0.031, 0.170, 0.140)) \
68	            and max(v.co.x for v in vs) - min(v.co.x for v in vs) < 0.006:
69	        LENS_FACES.update(comp)
70	src_bm.free()
71	print("PICK trigger faces", len(TRIGGER_FACES), "lens faces", len(LENS_FACES))
72	if not TRIGGER_FACES or not LENS_FACES:
73	    raise SystemExit("rifle_export_fbx: trigger or lens panels not found")
74	
75	
76	def set_imbue_uv(bm):
77	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("ImbueU") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("ImbueU")
78	    for f in bm.faces:
79	        for loop in f.loops:
80	            co = loop.vert.co
81	            u = (co.y - STRIP_Y0) / (STRIP_Y1 - STRIP_Y0)
82	            strip = STRIP_Y0 <= co.y <= STRIP_Y1 and co.z < STRIP_ZMAX
83	            # V is flipped by the FBX import (Unreal V = 1 - Blender V): Unreal gets V = 0 on the strip, 1 off it.
84	            loop[uv].uv = (u, 1.0 if strip else 0.0)
85	
86	
87	def build(name, pivot, faces=None, material=None, extra=None, imbue=False, slot_materials=None):
88	    """One mesh: the source faces whose index is in faces (all if None), or only the extra geometry, moved so pivot is
89	    the origin and turned so the muzzle points to +X."""
90	    bm = bmesh.new()
91	    materials = slot_materials or ([material] if material is not None else list(SRC.data.materials))
92	    if faces is not None or extra is None:
93	        bm.from_mesh(SRC.data)
94	        bm.faces.ensure_lookup_table()
95	        if faces is not None:
96	            bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[f for f in bm.faces if f.index not in faces], context="FACES")
97	        if material is not None:
98	            for f in bm.faces:
99	                f.material_index = 0
100	    if extra is not None:
101	        extra(bm)
102	    if imbue:
103	        set_imbue_uv(bm)
104	    bm.transform(TURN @ Matrix.Translation(-pivot))
105	    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
106	    bm.to_mesh(me)
107	    bm.free()
108	    # The GLB's custom normals do not survive the bmesh round trip, and every face is smooth-shaded: the hard-surface
109	    # gun rendered soft and rounded (owner: "it looks made of jelly"). Hard edges above SHARP_ANGLE restore the panels.
110	    me.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=math.radians(SHARP_ANGLE))
111	    for m in materials:
112	        me.materials.append(m)
113	    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
114	    scene.collection.objects.link(ob)
115	    xs = [v.co.x for v in me.vertices]; ys = [v.co.y for v in me.vertices]; zs = [v.co.z for v in me.vertices]
116	    info = {"tris": sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in me.polygons),
117	            "min": [round(min(xs), 4), round(min(ys), 4), round(min(zs), 4)],
118	            "max": [round(max(xs), 4), round(max(ys), 4), round(max(zs), 4)],
119	            "materials": [m.name for m in materials], "uv_maps": [l.name for l in me.uv_layers],
120	            "offset_from_body": [round(v, 4) for v in (TURN.to_3x3() @ (pivot - HAND))]}
121	    print("PART", name, json.dumps(info))
122	    return ob, info
123	
124	
125	def export(ob):
126	    for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects:
127	        o.select_set(False)
128	    ob.select_set(True)
129	    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = ob
130	    path = os.path.join(out_dir, "Export", ob.name + ".fbx")
131	    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=path, use_selection=True, object_types={"MESH"}, apply_unit_scale=True,
132	                             apply_scale_options="FBX_SCALE_NONE", mesh_smooth_type="FACE", use_mesh_modifiers=False,
133	                             add_leaf_bones=False, bake_anim=False, use_custom_props=False, path_mode="STRIP",
134	                             axis_forward="-Z", axis_up="Y")
135	    print("WROTE", path)
136	
137	
138	# ---- the magazine (new geometry) ----
139	MAG_HALF_W = 0.0125
140	MAG_TOP_Z, MAG_BOTTOM_Z = -0.028, -0.163
141	MAG_TOP_Y = (0.006, 0.050)          # back and front faces at the top (front = smaller Y, towards the muzzle)
142	MAG_FORWARD = 0.04                  # how far the bottom curves towards the muzzle
143	MAG_RINGS = 8
144	
145	
146	def mag_section(t):
147	    """Front and back Y and the Z of the magazine at t (0 top, 1 bottom): a gentle forward curve."""
148	    z = MAG_TOP_Z + (MAG_BOTTOM_Z - MAG_TOP_Z) * t
149	    shift = MAG_FORWARD * t * t
150	    return MAG_TOP_Y[0] - shift, MAG_TOP_Y[1] - shift, z
151	
152	
153	def add_box_rings(bm, rings, mat):
154	    """rings: list of (y_front, y_back, z, half_w), top to bottom; a closed tube with caps."""
155	    loops = []
156	    for yf, yb, z, hw in rings:
157	        loops.append([bm.verts.new((CX - hw, yf, z)), bm.verts.new((CX + hw, yf, z)),
158	                      bm.verts.new((CX + hw, yb, z)), bm.verts.new((CX - hw, yb, z))])
159	    faces = []
160	    for a, b in zip(loops, loops[1:]):
161	        for i in range(4):
162	            j = (i + 1) % 4
163	            faces.append(bm.faces.new((a[i], a[j], b[j], b[i])))
164	    faces.append(bm.faces.new(loops[0]))
165	    faces.append(bm.faces.new(list(reversed(loops[-1]))))
166	    for f in faces:
167	        f.material_index = mat
168	    return faces
169	
170	
171	def add_magazine(bm):
172	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("UVMap") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
173	    rings = []
174	    for k in range(MAG_RINGS + 1):
175	        yf, yb, z = mag_section(k / MAG_RINGS)
176	        rings.append((yf, yb, z, MAG_HALF_W))
177	    body = add_box_rings(bm, rings, 0)
178	    # base plate: a little wider and longer, 9 mm tall
179	    yf, yb, z = mag_section(1.0)
180	    plate = add_box_rings(bm, [(yf - 0.004, yb + 0.004, z + 0.002, MAG_HALF_W + 0.0015),
181	                               (yf - 0.004, yb + 0.004, z - 0.007, MAG_HALF_W + 0.0015)], 1)
182	    # glowing round-counter slit on each side: a thin quad 0.4 mm proud of the side, from 25% to 80% of the length
183	    slit = []
184	    for side in (-1, 1):
185	        x = CX + side * (MAG_HALF_W + 0.0004)
186	        pts = []
187	        for t in (0.25, 0.8):
188	            yf, yb, z = mag_section(t)
189	            mid = (yf + yb) / 2
190	            pts.append((mid - 0.003, z)); pts.append((mid + 0.003, z))
191	        quad = [bm.verts.new((x, pts[0][0], pts[0][1])), bm.verts.new((x, pts[1][0], pts[1][1])),
192	                bm.verts.new((x, pts[3][0], pts[3][1])), bm.verts.new((x, pts[2][0], pts[2][1]))]
193	        f = bm.faces.new(quad)
194	        f.material_index = 2
195	        f.normal_update()
196	        if (f.normal.x > 0) != (side > 0):
197	            f.normal_flip()
198	        slit.append(f)
199	    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=body + plate)
200	    for f in bm.faces:
201	        for loop in f.loops:
202	            loop[uv].uv = (0.5, 0.5)
203	
204	
205	def add_display_plane(bm):
206	    """The ammo display: a 2:1 hologram pane 1.5 mm behind the rear face of the sight's eyepiece (Y = 0.211, facing +Y,
207	    the player), inside that face (X -0.0185 .. 0.0085, half a millimetre in from its edges). The first version spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main
208	    face and seen from the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight (owner: fix the imperfections).
209	    UV: U to the viewer's right (-X seen from behind), V up in Blender (down in Unreal), so a texture reads upright."""
210	    y, x0, x1, z0, z1 = 0.2125, -0.0185, 0.0085, 0.12175, 0.13525
211	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("UVMap") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
212	    vs = [bm.verts.new((x, y, z)) for x, z in [(x0, z0), (x1, z0), (x1, z1), (x0, z1)]]
213	    face = bm.faces.new(vs)
214	    face.normal_update()
215	    if face.normal.y < 0:
216	        face.normal_flip()
217	    for loop in face.loops:
218	        co = loop.vert.co
219	        loop[uv].uv = ((x1 - co.x) / (x1 - x0), (co.z - z0) / (z1 - z0))
220	
221	
222	# Slot-naming materials for import_rifle.py (not used in Blender renders).
223	def mat(name):
224	    return bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)
225	
226	
227	all_faces = set(range(len(SRC.data.polygons)))
228	report = {"hand_point_source": [round(v, 4) for v in HAND], "parts": {}}
229	for name, pivot, kwargs in [
230	        ("SM_Rifle_Body", HAND, {"faces": all_faces - TRIGGER_FACES - LENS_FACES, "imbue": True}),
231	        ("SM_Rifle_Trigger", TRIGGER_PIVOT, {"faces": TRIGGER_FACES, "imbue": True}),
232	        ("SM_Rifle_WeakPointLight", HAND, {"faces": LENS_FACES, "material": mat("Rifle_WeakPoint")}),
233	        ("SM_Rifle_AmmoDisplay", HAND, {"extra": add_display_plane, "material": mat("Holo_AmmoDisplay")}),
234	]:
235	    ob, info = build(name, pivot, **kwargs)
236	    report["parts"][name] = info
237	    export(ob)
238	
239	# The magazine has three slots: body, base plate, glowing slit.
240	bm_mats = [mat("Rifle_Mag_Body"), mat("Rifle_Mag_Plate"), mat("Rifle_Mag_Glow")]
241	ob, info = build("SM_Rifle_Magazine", MAG_PIVOT, extra=add_magazine, slot_materials=bm_mats)
242	report["parts"]["SM_Rifle_Magazine"] = info
243	export(ob)
244	
245	report["magazine_out_offset"] = [round(v, 4) for v in (TURN.to_3x3() @ MAG_OUT)]
246	report["strip_y_source"] = [STRIP_Y0, STRIP_Y1]
247

# Exports the assault rifle (Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend, one Tripo mesh made of ~1000 loose
# panels) as static-mesh FBX files for Unreal, plus its two textures. The game animates the moving parts in code.
#   SM_Rifle_Body            everything that does not move. UV 1 ("ImbueU") drives the energy strip: U = 0 at the
#                            muzzle end of the side neon strip, 1 at its rear end; V = 1 marks glow that is not part of
#                            the strip (always lit). M_RifleAtlas splits the strip into 13 cells, like the pistol bar.
#   SM_Rifle_Trigger         the trigger blade inside the guard, pivot at its top (hinge)
#   SM_Rifle_Magazine        NEW geometry modelled here (the source has no magazine): a curved box magazine under the
#                            magazine well in front of the trigger guard, base plate and a glowing slit on each side
#   SM_Rifle_WeakPointLight  the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight (lit only on weak-point hits)
#   SM_Rifle_AmmoDisplay     a 2:1 quad just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player, for the ammo count
# Source frame: muzzle at -Y, up +Z, metres, ~1.0 m long. Export frame: turned +90 deg around Z so the muzzle points
# to +X (Unreal forward), origin at the hand point (top of the pistol grip). Same FBX settings as the pistol.
# Usage: blender -b Rifle.blend --python rifle_export_fbx.py -- <out_dir>
import bpy, bmesh, sys, os, json, math
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
out_dir = argv[0]
os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "Export"), exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "Textures"), exist_ok=True)

scene = bpy.context.scene
SRC = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"][0]
CX = -0.0055                       # the model's centre line in X (its left and right panels mirror around it)
HAND = Vector((CX, 0.19, 0.0))     # top of the pistol grip
TRIGGER_PIVOT = Vector((CX, 0.125, 0.003))
MAG_PIVOT = Vector((CX, 0.032, -0.028))
MAG_OUT = Vector((0.0, -0.02, -0.17))   # slide-out vector of the magazine on reload, source frame
TURN = Matrix.Rotation(math.pi / 2, 4, "Z")
SHARP_ANGLE = 30.0   # degrees: edges sharper than this are shaded hard
# Neon strip span along Y (source frame): from its muzzle end to its rear end, below the sight.
STRIP_Y0, STRIP_Y1, STRIP_ZMAX = -0.345, 0.085, 0.1


def islands(bm):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for f in bm.faces:
        if f.index in seen:
            continue
        stack, comp = [f], []
        seen.add(f.index)
        while stack:
            a = stack.pop()
            comp.append(a.index)
            for e in a.edges:
                for b in e.link_faces:
                    if b.index not in seen:
                        seen.add(b.index)
                        stack.append(b)
        out.append(comp)
    return out


def inside(vs, lo, hi):
    return all(lo[i] <= min(v.co[i] for v in vs) and max(v.co[i] for v in vs) <= hi[i] for i in range(3))


# Pick the trigger and the lenses by the bounding box of their loose panels.
src_bm = bmesh.new()
src_bm.from_mesh(SRC.data)
src_bm.faces.ensure_lookup_table()
TRIGGER_FACES, LENS_FACES = set(), set()
for comp in islands(src_bm):
    vs = {v for i in comp for v in src_bm.faces[i].verts}
    if inside(vs, (-0.0105, 0.116, -0.043), (-0.0005, 0.134, 0.0035)):
        TRIGGER_FACES.update(comp)
    elif len(comp) >= 15 and inside(vs, (-0.042, 0.104, 0.105), (0.031, 0.170, 0.140)) \
            and max(v.co.x for v in vs) - min(v.co.x for v in vs) < 0.006:
        LENS_FACES.update(comp)
src_bm.free()
print("PICK trigger faces", len(TRIGGER_FACES), "lens faces", len(LENS_FACES))
if not TRIGGER_FACES or not LENS_FACES:
    raise SystemExit("rifle_export_fbx: trigger or lens panels not found")


def set_imbue_uv(bm):
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("ImbueU") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("ImbueU")
    for f in bm.faces:
        for loop in f.loops:
            co = loop.vert.co
            u = (co.y - STRIP_Y0) / (STRIP_Y1 - STRIP_Y0)
            strip = STRIP_Y0 <= co.y <= STRIP_Y1 and co.z < STRIP_ZMAX
            # V is flipped by the FBX import (Unreal V = 1 - Blender V): Unreal gets V = 0 on the strip, 1 off it.
            loop[uv].uv = (u, 1.0 if strip else 0.0)


def build(name, pivot, faces=None, material=None, extra=None, imbue=False, slot_materials=None):
    """One mesh: the source faces whose index is in faces (all if None), or only the extra geometry, moved so pivot is
    the origin and turned so the muzzle points to +X."""
    bm = bmesh.new()
    materials = slot_materials or ([material] if material is not None else list(SRC.data.materials))
    if faces is not None or extra is None:
        bm.from_mesh(SRC.data)
        bm.faces.ensure_lookup_table()
        if faces is not None:
            bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[f for f in bm.faces if f.index not in faces], context="FACES")
        if material is not None:
            for f in bm.faces:
                f.material_index = 0
    if extra is not None:
        extra(bm)
    if imbue:
        set_imbue_uv(bm)
    bm.transform(TURN @ Matrix.Translation(-pivot))
    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()
    # The GLB's custom normals do not survive the bmesh round trip, and every face is smooth-shaded: the hard-surface
    # gun rendered soft and rounded (owner: "it looks made of jelly"). Hard edges above SHARP_ANGLE restore the panels.
    me.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=math.radians(SHARP_ANGLE))
    for m in materials:
        me.materials.append(m)
    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
    scene.collection.objects.link(ob)
    xs = [v.co.x for v in me.vertices]; ys = [v.co.y for v in me.vertices]; zs = [v.co.z for v in me.vertices]
    info = {"tris": sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in me.polygons),
            "min": [round(min(xs), 4), round(min(ys), 4), round(min(zs), 4)],
            "max": [round(max(xs), 4), round(max(ys), 4), round(max(zs), 4)],
            "materials": [m.name for m in materials], "uv_maps": [l.name for l in me.uv_layers],
            "offset_from_body": [round(v, 4) for v in (TURN.to_3x3() @ (pivot - HAND))]}
    print("PART", name, json.dumps(info))
    return ob, info


def export(ob):
    for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects:
        o.select_set(False)
    ob.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = ob
    path = os.path.join(out_dir, "Export", ob.name + ".fbx")
    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=path, use_selection=True, object_types={"MESH"}, apply_unit_scale=True,
                             apply_scale_options="FBX_SCALE_NONE", mesh_smooth_type="FACE", use_mesh_modifiers=False,
                             add_leaf_bones=False, bake_anim=False, use_custom_props=False, path_mode="STRIP",
                             axis_forward="-Z", axis_up="Y")
    print("WROTE", path)


# ---- the magazine (new geometry) ----
MAG_HALF_W = 0.0125
MAG_TOP_Z, MAG_BOTTOM_Z = -0.028, -0.163
MAG_TOP_Y = (0.006, 0.050)          # back and front faces at the top (front = smaller Y, towards the muzzle)
MAG_FORWARD = 0.04                  # how far the bottom curves towards the muzzle
MAG_RINGS = 8


def mag_section(t):
    """Front and back Y and the Z of the magazine at t (0 top, 1 bottom): a gentle forward curve."""
    z = MAG_TOP_Z + (MAG_BOTTOM_Z - MAG_TOP_Z) * t
    shift = MAG_FORWARD * t * t
    return MAG_TOP_Y[0] - shift, MAG_TOP_Y[1] - shift, z


def add_box_rings(bm, rings, mat):
    """rings: list of (y_front, y_back, z, half_w), top to bottom; a closed tube with caps."""
    loops = []
    for yf, yb, z, hw in rings:
        loops.append([bm.verts.new((CX - hw, yf, z)), bm.verts.new((CX + hw, yf, z)),
                      bm.verts.new((CX + hw, yb, z)), bm.verts.new((CX - hw, yb, z))])
    faces = []
    for a, b in zip(loops, loops[1:]):
        for i in range(4):
            j = (i + 1) % 4
            faces.append(bm.faces.new((a[i], a[j], b[j], b[i])))
    faces.append(bm.faces.new(loops[0]))
    faces.append(bm.faces.new(list(reversed(loops[-1]))))
    for f in faces:
        f.material_index = mat
    return faces


def add_magazine(bm):
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("UVMap") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
    rings = []
    for k in range(MAG_RINGS + 1):
        yf, yb, z = mag_section(k / MAG_RINGS)
        rings.append((yf, yb, z, MAG_HALF_W))
    body = add_box_rings(bm, rings, 0)
    # base plate: a little wider and longer, 9 mm tall
    yf, yb, z = mag_section(1.0)
    plate = add_box_rings(bm, [(yf - 0.004, yb + 0.004, z + 0.002, MAG_HALF_W + 0.0015),
                               (yf - 0.004, yb + 0.004, z - 0.007, MAG_HALF_W + 0.0015)], 1)
    # glowing round-counter slit on each side: a thin quad 0.4 mm proud of the side, from 25% to 80% of the length
    slit = []
    for side in (-1, 1):
        x = CX + side * (MAG_HALF_W + 0.0004)
        pts = []
        for t in (0.25, 0.8):
            yf, yb, z = mag_section(t)
            mid = (yf + yb) / 2
            pts.append((mid - 0.003, z)); pts.append((mid + 0.003, z))
        quad = [bm.verts.new((x, pts[0][0], pts[0][1])), bm.verts.new((x, pts[1][0], pts[1][1])),
                bm.verts.new((x, pts[3][0], pts[3][1])), bm.verts.new((x, pts[2][0], pts[2][1]))]
        f = bm.faces.new(quad)
        f.material_index = 2
        f.normal_update()
        if (f.normal.x > 0) != (side > 0):
            f.normal_flip()
        slit.append(f)
    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=body + plate)
    for f in bm.faces:
        for loop in f.loops:
            loop[uv].uv = (0.5, 0.5)


def add_display_plane(bm):
    """The ammo display: a 2:1 hologram pane 1.5 mm behind the rear face of the sight's eyepiece (Y = 0.211, facing +Y,
    the player), inside that face (X -0.0185 .. 0.0085, half a millimetre in from its edges). The first version spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main
    face and seen from the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight (owner: fix the imperfections).
    UV: U to the viewer's right (-X seen from behind), V up in Blender (down in Unreal), so a texture reads upright."""
    y, x0, x1, z0, z1 = 0.2125, -0.0185, 0.0085, 0.12175, 0.13525
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("UVMap") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
    vs = [bm.verts.new((x, y, z)) for x, z in [(x0, z0), (x1, z0), (x1, z1), (x0, z1)]]
    face = bm.faces.new(vs)
    face.normal_update()
    if face.normal.y < 0:
        face.normal_flip()
    for loop in face.loops:
        co = loop.vert.co
        loop[uv].uv = ((x1 - co.x) / (x1 - x0), (co.z - z0) / (z1 - z0))


# Slot-naming materials for import_rifle.py (not used in Blender renders).
def mat(name):
    return bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)


all_faces = set(range(len(SRC.data.polygons)))
report = {"hand_point_source": [round(v, 4) for v in HAND], "parts": {}}
for name, pivot, kwargs in [
        ("SM_Rifle_Body", HAND, {"faces": all_faces - TRIGGER_FACES - LENS_FACES, "imbue": True}),
        ("SM_Rifle_Trigger", TRIGGER_PIVOT, {"faces": TRIGGER_FACES, "imbue": True}),
        ("SM_Rifle_WeakPointLight", HAND, {"faces": LENS_FACES, "material": mat("Rifle_WeakPoint")}),
        ("SM_Rifle_AmmoDisplay", HAND, {"extra": add_display_plane, "material": mat("Holo_AmmoDisplay")}),
]:
    ob, info = build(name, pivot, **kwargs)
    report["parts"][name] = info
    export(ob)

# The magazine has three slots: body, base plate, glowing slit.
bm_mats = [mat("Rifle_Mag_Body"), mat("Rifle_Mag_Plate"), mat("Rifle_Mag_Glow")]
ob, info = build("SM_Rifle_Magazine", MAG_PIVOT, extra=add_magazine, slot_materials=bm_mats)
report["parts"]["SM_Rifle_Magazine"] = info
export(ob)

report["magazine_out_offset"] = [round(v, 4) for v in (TURN.to_3x3() @ MAG_OUT)]
report["strip_y_source"] = [STRIP_Y0, STRIP_Y1]

# Textures: the Tripo albedo and its neon mask, as PNG.
for image_name, out_name in [(next(i.name for i in bpy.data.images if i.name.startswith("Color_")), "T_Rifle_BaseColor"),
                             ("neon_mask", "T_Rifle_EmissiveMask")]:
    im = bpy.data.images[image_name].copy()
    im.filepath_raw = os.path.join(out_dir, "Textures", out_name + ".png")
    im.file_format = "PNG"
    im.save()
    print("TEXTURE", out_name)

with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "export_report.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
print("REPORT", json.dumps(report))

# Imports the rifle GLB into an empty scene, packs its images and saves it as the one source .blend.
# Usage: blender -b --factory-startup --python rifle_import_glb.py -- <model.glb> <out.blend>
import bpy, sys
argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
glb, out = argv[0], argv[1]
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=glb)
for im in bpy.data.images:
    if im.packed_file is None and im.size[0] > 0:
        im.pack()
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=out)
print("SAVED", out)

241	## Sixteenth block: the assault rifle, from one Tripo mesh to a complete weapon
242	Owner's note (translated): "This is the game's assault rifle. I think it's a single mesh, and all the work it needs is ahead of it; you will do it. Animations, the colour change, the ammo panel, everything as you already know: it has to end up as a complete and absolutely functional weapon, with everything a game of this kind needs. Modify it in Blender or Unreal as you like. For code tasks, don't use Muse Spark, use Sonnet."
243	
244	**The source.** The owner's `carabina-roja.zip` held a Tripo GLB. It is one mesh of about 1,000 loose panels and 5,498 triangles, 1.0 m long. It came with a 4096 albedo and a `neon_mask` that marks where it glows.
245	- It had **no magazine** and no separate moving parts.
246	- The architect (Claude Opus 5.5) did the art headless in Blender 5.3.0, without asking. Scripts:
247	  - `Tools/Blender/rifle_import_glb.py`: GLB to `SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend`, the one source;
248	  - `rifle_export_fbx.py`;
249	  - `Tools/Jam/Import-Rifle.ps1` and `import_rifle.py`, with the same one-source rule as the pistol.
250	
251	**The parts and how each was chosen.** The rifle has five meshes in `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Rifle`.
252	- **Trigger:** the blade's panels, picked by their bounding box inside the guard. Its origin is at the hinge, so it rotates -8° like the pistol's.
253	- **Magazine:** new geometry modelled by script, because the model had none and a rifle needs one to reload.
254	  - A curved box under the stub in front of the trigger guard, with a base plate.
255	  - A glowing slit on each side, in the element colour.
256	  - On reload it slides out 17 cm, then back in.
257	- **Weak-point light:** the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight. They are off normally and flash on a head or weak-point hit, the pistol's rule.
258	- **Ammo display:** a 2:1 hologram pane just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player. It is the pistol's shared `M_GunHolo`, with its own text layout: no frame or dots to avoid, so the number is larger.
259	- **Energy bar:** no separate mesh. The body's second UV map carries the position along the side neon strip, and `M_RifleAtlas` cuts the strip into 13 cells with thin dark gaps.
260	  - They drain from the muzzle end with the enchant's time left: the same "+ half a cell" rule and the same code as the pistol.
261	  - The rest of the neon glows in the element colour all the time: idle mint (the model's own colour), or the enchant's element.
262	- **Problems found by the import checks:**
263	  - The FBX import flips V, so the "on the strip" flag in UV 1 came out inverted. The check that counts strip vertices caught it.
264	  - The magazine's three material slots collapsed into one. A new check now requires 3 slots.
265	  - Both were fixed in the export script before any code used them.
266	- **Textures:** the 4096 maps are capped at 2048 in Unreal.
267	
268	**Code: Claude Sonnet 5.5 at High effort.** The owner set it as the implementer for this chat, so not Muse Spark. Brief: `Prompts/feedback12_rifle_viewmodel.md`.
269	- The pistol-only viewmodel code became one code path for both guns. A small art description per model (folder, parts, offsets, scale, idle glow, muzzle tip, display layout) is chosen by `ViewModel` in `Weapons.json`.
270	- New for both guns:
271	  - **Shot kick:** the viewmodel moves back and tips up, then eases back over 0.09 s. It is the look only; aim and camera are untouched.
272	  - **Muzzle flash:** a 0.05 s glowing star at the muzzle in the glow colour.
273	- The rifle sits at scale 0.62, tuned by Sonnet over several smoke screenshots.
274	- The smoke run has new rifle steps, all green:
275	  - `meshes=5`;
276	  - display `30` → `29` → `--`;
277	  - magazine out 17.1 cm;
278	  - weak-point flash 1.00 → 0.00, and 0.00 on a body shot;
279	  - half bar 0.52;
280	  - muzzle flash and kick on both guns.
281	  - Every pistol line is unchanged.
282	- One deviation, reported by Sonnet: the smoke run applies the rifle's enchant as a status directly, because the enchant spell is still on cooldown from the pistol step.
283	- The architect looked at the screenshots: the rifle is in the lower right, the number reads upright, and the flash sits at the muzzle. Accepted.
284	- **Owner, after the screenshot (translated):** "The rifle closer to the screen", then "the front pointing at the crosshair, a little closer and to the left". Done directly by the architect, because these are values in the rifle's art description:
285	  - root offset (30, 2, 1) → (14, 2, 1) → (8, -3, 2) cm;
286	  - yaw -5° → -10°;
287	  - checked on `media/2026-11-12/14b_rifle_hip_closer.png`: the barrel now runs to the crosshair, and "30" is about twice as large.
288	- Package `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`: 252.8 MB.
289	- **Owner, second note (translated):** "The weapon is still too far away in the frame, bring it closer. Its alignment doesn't go straight to the crosshair: look at how rifles are framed in first-person shooters and adjust it. And look closely at the screenshots you sent: there are still imperfections on the rifle; find them and fix them."
290	  - **Framing.** The architect searched the web: Unreal answers, Leadwerks and Roblox developer threads, and CS2 viewmodel guides. At the hip, the weapon is held parallel to the view, or turned slightly towards the point the crosshair aims at. Perspective then makes the barrel converge on the screen centre. Our -10° yaw made the barrel cross the crosshair instead.
291	    - The rifle is now parallel to the view (yaw -0.4°, the angle that meets the crosshair at 15 m), 20 cm closer and 3 cm further left: root offset (-12, -6, 2) cm.
292	    - The barrel line now runs into the crosshair, and the sight with its ammo count sits in the lower right.
293	  - **Imperfections the architect found on enlarged crops of the screenshots, and the fixes:**
294	    1. The hologram pane spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main face. From the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight. It is now inside the rear face of the eyepiece, 1.5 mm in front of it.
295	    2. Right after the rifle was equipped it looked flat, blurry and tan: textures still streaming in at their lowest mip. The two rifle textures are now never streamed (about 5 MB resident).
296	    3. The 10 cm near plane cut the stock open at the bottom right. It is now 3 cm (`DefaultEngine.ini`, `NearClipPlane`), the usual fix for first-person weapons.
297	    4. The white polymer read washed out next to the pistol: albedo × 0.8.
298	  - **Tried and reverted:** a two-sided material, to guard against holes in the loose-panel mesh. The Tripo panels are doubled back to back and z-fought, so the whole rifle looked grainy. It stays one-sided, with the reason written in `import_rifle.py`.
299	  - Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/14c_rifle_hip_framed.png` (idle) and `14d_rifle_enchanted.png` (lightning enchant, half bar).
300	- **Owner, third note (translated):** "In the screenshots you sent, the weapon looks like it's made of jelly." The architect found three causes:
301	  1. **Lost normals.** The Tripo GLB carries custom normals, and the export's bmesh round trip dropped them. Every face was then smooth-shaded, so the hard-surface gun rendered soft and rounded. Fix: edges sharper than 30° are now shaded hard (`set_sharp_from_angle` in `rifle_export_fbx.py`).
302	  2. **One flat material value.** Roughness 0.42 and metallic 0.15 covered the whole gun, so it looked soft and glossy. The source has no roughness map. The albedo's brightness now tells polymer from metal: light parts are matte polymer (roughness 0.68, not metallic), dark parts satin metal (0.36, metallic 0.6).
303	  3. **No self-shadow.** The viewmodel parts cast no shadow at all, so nothing shaded anything else. They are now "self shadow only": the gun shades itself (the sight now drops a shadow on the receiver) but casts nothing on the world. This applies to the pistol too; checked on `13a`, which is unchanged apart from its own shading.
304	  - The rifle textures went back to full 4096 (no streaming), because the parts nearest the camera were blurry at 2048. The package grew from 252.8 to 256 MB.
305	  - **Note on the smoke screenshots:** `14a` comes out tan and grainy whenever the rifle material has just changed. That is the editor's fallback material while shaders compile. The packaged game ships compiled shaders, so it does not happen there.
306	  - Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/14f_rifle_solid.png`, `14g_rifle_solid_enchanted.png`.
307	- **To check by playing:**
308	  - The framing. The stock now goes under the HUD weapon box at the bottom right.
309	  - Whether "30" is readable.
310	  - The look while aiming.
311	  - The feel of full-auto kick.
312	  - The strip draining over a real enchant.

1	# Exports the assault rifle (Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend, one Tripo mesh made of ~1000 loose
2	# panels) as static-mesh FBX files for Unreal, plus its two textures. The game animates the moving parts in code.
3	#   SM_Rifle_Body            everything that does not move. UV 1 ("ImbueU") drives the energy strip: U = 0 at the
4	#                            muzzle end of the side neon strip, 1 at its rear end; V = 1 marks glow that is not part of
5	#                            the strip (always lit). M_RifleAtlas splits the strip into 13 cells, like the pistol bar.
6	#   SM_Rifle_Trigger         the trigger blade inside the guard, pivot at its top (hinge)
7	#   SM_Rifle_Magazine        NEW geometry modelled here (the source has no magazine): a curved box magazine under the
8	#                            magazine well in front of the trigger guard, base plate and a glowing slit on each side
9	#   SM_Rifle_WeakPointLight  the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight (lit only on weak-point hits)
10	#   SM_Rifle_AmmoDisplay     a 2:1 quad just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player, for the ammo count
11	# Source frame: muzzle at -Y, up +Z, metres, ~1.0 m long. Export frame: turned +90 deg around Z so the muzzle points
12	# to +X (Unreal forward), origin at the hand point (top of the pistol grip). Same FBX settings as the pistol.
13	# Usage: blender -b Rifle.blend --python rifle_export_fbx.py -- <out_dir>
14	import bpy, bmesh, sys, os, json, math
15	from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
16	
17	argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
18	out_dir = argv[0]
19	os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "Export"), exist_ok=True)
20	os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "Textures"), exist_ok=True)
21	
22	scene = bpy.context.scene
23	SRC = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"][0]
24	CX = -0.0055                       # the model's centre line in X (its left and right panels mirror around it)
25	HAND = Vector((CX, 0.19, 0.0))     # top of the pistol grip
26	TRIGGER_PIVOT = Vector((CX, 0.125, 0.003))
27	MAG_PIVOT = Vector((CX, 0.032, -0.028))
28	MAG_OUT = Vector((0.0, -0.02, -0.17))   # slide-out vector of the magazine on reload, source frame
29	TURN = Matrix.Rotation(math.pi / 2, 4, "Z")
30	SHARP_ANGLE = 30.0   # degrees: edges sharper than this are shaded hard
31	# Neon strip span along Y (source frame): from its muzzle end to its rear end, below the sight.
32	STRIP_Y0, STRIP_Y1, STRIP_ZMAX = -0.345, 0.085, 0.1
33	
34	
35	def islands(bm):
36	    seen, out = set(), []
37	    for f in bm.faces:
38	        if f.index in seen:
39	            continue
40	        stack, comp = [f], []
41	        seen.add(f.index)
42	        while stack:
43	            a = stack.pop()
44	            comp.append(a.index)
45	            for e in a.edges:
46	                for b in e.link_faces:
47	                    if b.index not in seen:
48	                        seen.add(b.index)
49	                        stack.append(b)
50	        out.append(comp)
51	    return out
52	
53	
54	def inside(vs, lo, hi):
55	    return all(lo[i] <= min(v.co[i] for v in vs) and max(v.co[i] for v in vs) <= hi[i] for i in range(3))
56	
57	
58	# Pick the trigger and the lenses by the bounding box of their loose panels.
59	src_bm = bmesh.new()
60	src_bm.from_mesh(SRC.data)
61	src_bm.faces.ensure_lookup_table()
62	TRIGGER_FACES, LENS_FACES = set(), set()
63	for comp in islands(src_bm):
64	    vs = {v for i in comp for v in src_bm.faces[i].verts}
65	    if inside(vs, (-0.0105, 0.116, -0.043), (-0.0005, 0.134, 0.0035)):
66	        TRIGGER_FACES.update(comp)
67	    elif len(comp) >= 15 and inside(vs, (-0.042, 0.104, 0.105), (0.031, 0.170, 0.140)) \
68	            and max(v.co.x for v in vs) - min(v.co.x for v in vs) < 0.006:
69	        LENS_FACES.update(comp)
70	src_bm.free()
71	print("PICK trigger faces", len(TRIGGER_FACES), "lens faces", len(LENS_FACES))
72	if not TRIGGER_FACES or not LENS_FACES:
73	    raise SystemExit("rifle_export_fbx: trigger or lens panels not found")
74	
75	
76	def set_imbue_uv(bm):
77	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("ImbueU") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("ImbueU")
78	    for f in bm.faces:
79	        for loop in f.loops:
80	            co = loop.vert.co
81	            u = (co.y - STRIP_Y0) / (STRIP_Y1 - STRIP_Y0)
82	            strip = STRIP_Y0 <= co.y <= STRIP_Y1 and co.z < STRIP_ZMAX
83	            # V is flipped by the FBX import (Unreal V = 1 - Blender V): Unreal gets V = 0 on the strip, 1 off it.
84	            loop[uv].uv = (u, 1.0 if strip else 0.0)
85	
86	
87	def build(name, pivot, faces=None, material=None, extra=None, imbue=False, slot_materials=None):
88	    """One mesh: the source faces whose index is in faces (all if None), or only the extra geometry, moved so pivot is
89	    the origin and turned so the muzzle points to +X."""
90	    bm = bmesh.new()
91	    materials = slot_materials or ([material] if material is not None else list(SRC.data.materials))
92	    if faces is not None or extra is None:
93	        bm.from_mesh(SRC.data)
94	        bm.faces.ensure_lookup_table()
95	        if faces is not None:
96	            bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[f for f in bm.faces if f.index not in faces], context="FACES")
97	        if material is not None:
98	            for f in bm.faces:
99	                f.material_index = 0
100	    if extra is not None:
101	        extra(bm)
102	    if imbue:
103	        set_imbue_uv(bm)
104	    bm.transform(TURN @ Matrix.Translation(-pivot))
105	    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
106	    bm.to_mesh(me)
107	    bm.free()
108	    # The GLB's custom normals do not survive the bmesh round trip, and every face is smooth-shaded: the hard-surface
109	    # gun rendered soft and rounded (owner: "it looks made of jelly"). Hard edges above SHARP_ANGLE restore the panels.
110	    me.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=math.radians(SHARP_ANGLE))
111	    for m in materials:
112	        me.materials.append(m)
113	    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
114	    scene.collection.objects.link(ob)
115	    xs = [v.co.x for v in me.vertices]; ys = [v.co.y for v in me.vertices]; zs = [v.co.z for v in me.vertices]
116	    info = {"tris": sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in me.polygons),
117	            "min": [round(min(xs), 4), round(min(ys), 4), round(min(zs), 4)],
118	            "max": [round(max(xs), 4), round(max(ys), 4), round(max(zs), 4)],
119	            "materials": [m.name for m in materials], "uv_maps": [l.name for l in me.uv_layers],
120	            "offset_from_body": [round(v, 4) for v in (TURN.to_3x3() @ (pivot - HAND))]}
121	    print("PART", name, json.dumps(info))
122	    return ob, info
123	
124	
125	def export(ob):
126	    for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects:
127	        o.select_set(False)
128	    ob.select_set(True)
129	    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = ob
130	    path = os.path.join(out_dir, "Export", ob.name + ".fbx")
131	    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=path, use_selection=True, object_types={"MESH"}, apply_unit_scale=True,
132	                             apply_scale_options="FBX_SCALE_NONE", mesh_smooth_type="FACE", use_mesh_modifiers=False,
133	                             add_leaf_bones=False, bake_anim=False, use_custom_props=False, path_mode="STRIP",
134	                             axis_forward="-Z", axis_up="Y")
135	    print("WROTE", path)
136	
137	
138	# ---- the magazine (new geometry) ----
139	MAG_HALF_W = 0.0125
140	MAG_TOP_Z, MAG_BOTTOM_Z = -0.028, -0.163
141	MAG_TOP_Y = (0.006, 0.050)          # back and front faces at the top (front = smaller Y, towards the muzzle)
142	MAG_FORWARD = 0.04                  # how far the bottom curves towards the muzzle
143	MAG_RINGS = 8
144	
145	
146	def mag_section(t):
147	    """Front and back Y and the Z of the magazine at t (0 top, 1 bottom): a gentle forward curve."""
148	    z = MAG_TOP_Z + (MAG_BOTTOM_Z - MAG_TOP_Z) * t
149	    shift = MAG_FORWARD * t * t
150	    return MAG_TOP_Y[0] - shift, MAG_TOP_Y[1] - shift, z
151	
152	
153	def add_box_rings(bm, rings, mat):
154	    """rings: list of (y_front, y_back, z, half_w), top to bottom; a closed tube with caps."""
155	    loops = []
156	    for yf, yb, z, hw in rings:
157	        loops.append([bm.verts.new((CX - hw, yf, z)), bm.verts.new((CX + hw, yf, z)),
158	                      bm.verts.new((CX + hw, yb, z)), bm.verts.new((CX - hw, yb, z))])
159	    faces = []
160	    for a, b in zip(loops, loops[1:]):
161	        for i in range(4):
162	            j = (i + 1) % 4
163	            faces.append(bm.faces.new((a[i], a[j], b[j], b[i])))
164	    faces.append(bm.faces.new(loops[0]))
165	    faces.append(bm.faces.new(list(reversed(loops[-1]))))
166	    for f in faces:
167	        f.material_index = mat
168	    return faces
169	
170	
171	def add_magazine(bm):
172	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("UVMap") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
173	    rings = []
174	    for k in range(MAG_RINGS + 1):
175	        yf, yb, z = mag_section(k / MAG_RINGS)
176	        rings.append((yf, yb, z, MAG_HALF_W))
177	    body = add_box_rings(bm, rings, 0)
178	    # base plate: a little wider and longer, 9 mm tall
179	    yf, yb, z = mag_section(1.0)
180	    plate = add_box_rings(bm, [(yf - 0.004, yb + 0.004, z + 0.002, MAG_HALF_W + 0.0015),
181	                               (yf - 0.004, yb + 0.004, z - 0.007, MAG_HALF_W + 0.0015)], 1)
182	    # glowing round-counter slit on each side: a thin quad 0.4 mm proud of the side, from 25% to 80% of the length
183	    slit = []
184	    for side in (-1, 1):
185	        x = CX + side * (MAG_HALF_W + 0.0004)
186	        pts = []
187	        for t in (0.25, 0.8):
188	            yf, yb, z = mag_section(t)
189	            mid = (yf + yb) / 2
190	            pts.append((mid - 0.003, z)); pts.append((mid + 0.003, z))
191	        quad = [bm.verts.new((x, pts[0][0], pts[0][1])), bm.verts.new((x, pts[1][0], pts[1][1])),
192	                bm.verts.new((x, pts[3][0], pts[3][1])), bm.verts.new((x, pts[2][0], pts[2][1]))]
193	        f = bm.faces.new(quad)
194	        f.material_index = 2
195	        f.normal_update()
196	        if (f.normal.x > 0) != (side > 0):
197	            f.normal_flip()
198	        slit.append(f)
199	    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=body + plate)
200	    for f in bm.faces:
201	        for loop in f.loops:
202	            loop[uv].uv = (0.5, 0.5)
203	
204	
205	def add_display_plane(bm):
206	    """The ammo display: a 2:1 hologram pane 1.5 mm behind the rear face of the sight's eyepiece (Y = 0.211, facing +Y,
207	    the player), inside that face (X -0.0185 .. 0.0085, half a millimetre in from its edges). The first version spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main
208	    face and seen from the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight (owner: fix the imperfections).
209	    UV: U to the viewer's right (-X seen from behind), V up in Blender (down in Unreal), so a texture reads upright."""
210	    y, x0, x1, z0, z1 = 0.2125, -0.0185, 0.0085, 0.12175, 0.13525
211	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.get("UVMap") or bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
212	    vs = [bm.verts.new((x, y, z)) for x, z in [(x0, z0), (x1, z0), (x1, z1), (x0, z1)]]
213	    face = bm.faces.new(vs)
214	    face.normal_update()
215	    if face.normal.y < 0:
216	        face.normal_flip()
217	    for loop in face.loops:
218	        co = loop.vert.co
219	        loop[uv].uv = ((x1 - co.x) / (x1 - x0), (co.z - z0) / (z1 - z0))
220	
221	
222	# Slot-naming materials for import_rifle.py (not used in Blender renders).
223	def mat(name):
224	    return bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)
225	
226	
227	all_faces = set(range(len(SRC.data.polygons)))
228	report = {"hand_point_source": [round(v, 4) for v in HAND], "parts": {}}
229	for name, pivot, kwargs in [
230	        ("SM_Rifle_Body", HAND, {"faces": all_faces - TRIGGER_FACES - LENS_FACES, "imbue": True}),
231	        ("SM_Rifle_Trigger", TRIGGER_PIVOT, {"faces": TRIGGER_FACES, "imbue": True}),
232	        ("SM_Rifle_WeakPointLight", HAND, {"faces": LENS_FACES, "material": mat("Rifle_WeakPoint")}),
233	        ("SM_Rifle_AmmoDisplay", HAND, {"extra": add_display_plane, "material": mat("Holo_AmmoDisplay")}),
234	]:
235	    ob, info = build(name, pivot, **kwargs)
236	    report["parts"][name] = info
237	    export(ob)
238	
239	# The magazine has three slots: body, base plate, glowing slit.
240	bm_mats = [mat("Rifle_Mag_Body"), mat("Rifle_Mag_Plate"), mat("Rifle_Mag_Glow")]
241	ob, info = build("SM_Rifle_Magazine", MAG_PIVOT, extra=add_magazine, slot_materials=bm_mats)
242	report["parts"]["SM_Rifle_Magazine"] = info
243	export(ob)
244	
245	report["magazine_out_offset"] = [round(v, 4) for v in (TURN.to_3x3() @ MAG_OUT)]
246	report["strip_y_source"] = [STRIP_Y0, STRIP_Y1]
247	
248	# Textures: the Tripo albedo and its neon mask, as PNG.
249	for image_name, out_name in [(next(i.name for i in bpy.data.images if i.name.startswith("Color_")), "T_Rifle_BaseColor"),
250	                             ("neon_mask", "T_Rifle_EmissiveMask")]:
251	    im = bpy.data.images[image_name].copy()
252	    im.filepath_raw = os.path.join(out_dir, "Textures", out_name + ".png")
253	    im.file_format = "PNG"
254	    im.save()
255	    print("TEXTURE", out_name)
256	
257	with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "export_report.json"), "w") as f:
258	    json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
259	print("REPORT", json.dumps(report))

# Renders fixed review views of the pistol (both sides, top, front 3/4, approximate first-person) with EEVEE.
# Usage: blender -b <file.blend> --python pistol_render_views.py -- <out_dir> [frame] [res]
import bpy, sys, os, math
from mathutils import Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
out_dir = argv[0]
frame = int(argv[1]) if len(argv) > 1 else 1
res = int(argv[2]) if len(argv) > 2 else 1400
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

sc = bpy.context.scene
sc.frame_set(frame)
sc.render.engine = "BLENDER_EEVEE"
sc.render.resolution_x = res
sc.render.resolution_y = int(res * 0.75)
sc.render.film_transparent = False
sc.view_settings.view_transform = "AgX" if "AgX" in [i.identifier for i in sc.view_settings.bl_rna.properties["view_transform"].enum_items] else "Standard"

# neutral studio light, independent of whatever lights the file has
world = bpy.data.worlds.new("ReviewWorld")
world.use_nodes = True
bg = world.node_tree.nodes.get("Background")
bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.32, 0.33, 0.35, 1)
bg.inputs[1].default_value = 0.9
sc.world = world
for ob in list(bpy.data.objects):
    if ob.type == "LIGHT":
        ob.hide_render = True
def add_light(name, rot, energy):
    ld = bpy.data.lights.new(name, "SUN")
    ld.energy = energy
    lo = bpy.data.objects.new(name, ld)
    lo.rotation_euler = [math.radians(a) for a in rot]
    sc.collection.objects.link(lo)
add_light("Key", (50, 10, 35), 3.0)
add_light("Fill", (60, -10, 215), 1.2)

# bounds of all visible meshes
pts = []
for ob in sc.objects:
    if ob.type == "MESH" and not ob.hide_render:
        pts += [ob.matrix_world @ Vector(c) for c in ob.bound_box]
mn = Vector((min(p.x for p in pts), min(p.y for p in pts), min(p.z for p in pts)))
mx = Vector((max(p.x for p in pts), max(p.y for p in pts), max(p.z for p in pts)))
center = (mn + mx) / 2
size = (mx - mn).length

cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new("ReviewCam")
cam = bpy.data.objects.new("ReviewCam", cam_data)
sc.collection.objects.link(cam)
sc.camera = cam

def shoot(name, direction, dist_mul=1.25, lens=50, target=None):
    t = target if target is not None else center
    d = Vector(direction).normalized()
    cam.location = t + d * size * dist_mul
    cam.rotation_euler = (t - cam.location).to_track_quat("-Z", "Y").to_euler()
    cam_data.lens = lens
    sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{name}_f{frame:02d}.png")
    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
    print("RENDER", sc.render.filepath)

# The muzzle points to -X (the imbue bar's lit end is at low X). The energy bar is on the -Y side.
shoot("side_minusY", (0, -1, 0.05))
shoot("side_plusY", (0, 1, 0.05))
shoot("top", (0.0, -0.05, 1))
shoot("front34", (-1, -0.7, 0.35))
# approximate first-person: behind the grip (+X), slightly above and to the right
shoot("fps_approx", (1, -0.35, 0.45), dist_mul=0.75, lens=35)
